findings.consequence: The phase's '92 passed' does not hold on Linux x86-64 with AVX-512; Linux preflights of later phases fail. The implementation is numerically correct.
findings.statement: tests/test_phase1g_b_lagrangian_sigma.py line 428 asserts np.array_equal(W(-x), W(x)). NumPy's vectorised x**3 uses the X86_V4 (AVX-512) power kernel for positive bases (up to 0.61 ulp) and a correctly rounded path for negative bases, so (-x)**3 != -(x**3) in 51 of 997 points and W differs in 46 points by <= 3.3e-16 relative.
findings.suggested_resolution: Option A (test only): assert_allclose(W(-x), W(x), rtol=1e-15, atol=0.0) with a documented reason. Option B (implementation, output-preserving): evaluate the closed form on xl = np.abs(arr[~small]); bit-identical for all x > 0 (verified on 2.0e5 points), evenness exact, bitwise test kept. Recommend B.
findings.title: Window evenness test asserts bitwise sign symmetry of np.power; fails on Linux AVX-512

findings.statement: check_current_scientific_status iterates live tokens only: deleting a frozen token (even SIGMA8_AUTHORIZATION) from the live module passes silently. The EH98 validity range (trans.tex 686-687, 855-856) is not enforced (omega_m >= 9.83 gives s <= 0).
